newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanair expands domestic scheduled routes.
newsitem.headline: Spanair expands domestic scheduled routes.

text.p: Spanish independent carrier Spanair said it would inaugurate scheduled services from Madrid to Bilbao and Madrid to Malaga this winter, increasing the number of routes where it competes directly with the state-owned Iberia group.

A Spanair spokeswoman was unable to confirm further details, but market sources say the Palma de Mallorca-based carrier also plans to increase frequencies on its Madrid-Barcelona and Madrid-Santiago de Compostela services.
The company is 49 percent owned by Scandinavian Airlines System and has commercial ties with both SAS and its partner Deutsche Lufthansa AG.
Spanair recently signed a deal with Lufthansa to handle the German carrier's reservations in Spain outside normal office hours, the spokeswoman said.
